decision_rationale: The Commission–Member State payment and financial-protection relation is identifiable, and OLAF is institutionally distinct. Article 21 authorizes OLAF to exercise its own investigative and control rights but does not establish an object, transformation, output or recipient forming an R-to-OLAF-to-T chain. Removing OLAF removes a separate anti-fraud control function, not a mediating step in the underlying direct relation.

The direct Commission–Member State relation remains unchanged, but adjudicating the common auction platform as the third actor requires combining the operative reserve and calendar rules with recital 6, which identifies the platform. The full candidate role structure is therefore E2.

decision_rationale: The Member State–common auction platform relation requires Article 1(8) for the calendar consequence and recital 6 for explicit actor identity. Phase 6 was correct at E2; the Phase 5 E1 field required correction.
